p.i: In mare deducunt fessas erroribus undas.
Inachus unus abest, inoque reconditus antro
Fletibus auget aquas, natamque miserrimus Io
Luget, ut amissam: nescit vitane fruatur.
Æstuat Alphæus: ripa Sperchiades ardent.
Multa quoque Apidani placuerunt gramina ripis,
Multa quoque Amphrysi: nec eras immunis Enipeu.
Necnon Penæus, necnon Sperchiades unda
Contribuere aliquid, iuncosaque littora Bœbes,
Spercheusque, & virginibus bacchata Lacanis
Taygeta: o, qui me gelidis in vallibus Æmi
Sistat.
Palladiusque Melas, hecataq; gurgite nutrit
Gargaphye.
Littora contigerat, per quæ Penius amnis
Emathia iam clade rubens exibat in æquor.

main_text.head: Montes Thessaliæ præter Ossam & Pelion, qui tribuuntur ab aliis Macedoniæ, sunt Pindus, Pholoe, Thrachin, Oeta, Othrys.

p.i: Sublimis rapitur, subiectaque Thessala Tempe
Despicit, & visis regionibus applicat angues.

p.note: Montes Ossa. Pelion. Othrys. Pindus. Olympus.
p.i: Et quas Ossa tulit, quasque altus Pelion herbas,
Otryxq, & Pindus, & Pindo maior Olympus,
Perspicit, & placitas partim radice revellit,
Partim succidit curuamine falcis ahena.

main_text.head: Pindus.

note.i: Virg. egl.10. Horat.carm. lib.1. Seneca Hip- polytus.

p.i: Nam neque Parnassi vobis iuga, nam neque Pindi.
Aut super Pindo, gelidóve in Æmo.
Non me per altas ire, si iubeas, nines
Pigeat,

page.notes: Marginal notes are reproduced as printed; the reading of the faded left-margin references and the hyphenated line-ends is uncertain. The Greek word in "Otryxq" and some words in the verse may be misread. The last line is set at right and partly obscured by a tear at the lower edge.
